subject: From Meta to Nexar: Fireside Chat on AI @ CVPR
text:
Hi [NAME],

If you're around for CVPR, I'd love to personally invite you to a small
dinner we're hosting for a group of AI leaders on 06/14.

We'll kick off with a fireside chat with Luc Vincent-ex-VP of AI at Meta,
Chief R&D Officer at Nexar, and investor/advisor at Encord- followed by
dinner for AI leaders in Nashville on the Saturday of CVPR - we'd love for
you to join if you're interested / can make it!

Attendees are strictly reserved for senior leaders (CTOs, Heads of ML,
Co-founders) and we're headcount at ~25 guests from our existing Encord
partners and/or other leading AI/ML scale-ups and orgs - confirmed are
Toyota, Bosch and more.

A bit of context on Encord - we help over 200 AI teams improve data quality
for model development. We focus on consolidating data curation, annotation
and model evaluation with the goals of efficiency gains for training
dataset preparation & model iterations.

Let me know if you're interested/free - happy to send over the full details.

subject: CV Workflows for optical delousing
text:
Hi [NAME]​, 

Your system's use of stereo vision and laser targeting for delousing is one of the more advanced CV deployments I've seen in aquaculture - real-time inference in a turbulent, low-visibility environment is a serious challenge. 

At Encord, we support teams building high-precision, low-latency CV systems - helping them improve annotation speed, surface failure modes faster, and scale eval workflows as they iterate (FarmWise and Carbon Robotics). We've seen teams hit limits with tools like Voxel51 when accuracy or throughput becomes the bottleneck. 

Would you be up for a 20-min chat? I'd love to hear more about Stingray's approach and share what others in high-noise environments are doing.

subject: Accelerating 3D foundation model development
text:
Hi [NAME]​, 

Saw you're building out the London team - with NeRFs, splatting, and diffusion-based generation in focus, I imagine dataset curation, evaluation, and training iteration speed are top of mind. 

We've been working with teams like Runway and Woven to help streamline large-scale 3D and video pipelines: 
- surfacing edge cases across spatial/temporal data 
- integrating HITL loops for evaluating geometry, continuity, and realism 
- reducing overhead in feedback and re-training cycles 

If helpful, happy to share what we're seeing across similar GenAI teams building foundation models with complex 3D inputs. Tuesdays and Thursdays work well for me, if that suits.

subject: Scaling financial doc models: edge cases, ontologies, QA
text:
Hi [NAME]​, 

Saw [COMPANY]'s recent growth - imagine scaling your document understanding models is a priority as you expand automation across receipts, invoices, and travel docs. 

We've seen teams at companies like Hyperscience, Abbyy, and Rossum hit friction as internal tooling struggles to keep up with evolving document formats, compliance needs, and real-world variation. 

At Encord, we help teams streamline their pipelines - combining structured ontologies, LLM-assisted pre-labeling, and human-in-the-loop QA - so model development isn't bottlenecked by annotation overhead or brittle evaluation. 

Would you be open to a quick chat? Happy to share what's working for others in the space. Tuesdays or Thursdays usually best on my end.

text:
